claims.quote: Neuronal migration of glutamatergic neurons was impaired in the neocortices of KCNB1 null mice.

claims.object_text: migratory defects; disrupted morphology; disrupted synaptic connectivity
claims.quote: Migratory defects persisted into the adult brains, along with disrupted morphology and synaptic connectivity.
Mice developed seizure phenotype, anxiety, and compulsive behavior.

claims.object_text: Knock In (KI) mice harboring the gene variant Kcnb1R312H (R312H mice)
claims.quote: we constructed Knock In (KI) mice, harboring the gene variant Kcnb1R312H (R312H mice) found in children with developmental and epileptic encephalopathies (DEEs).

claims.object_text: developmental and epileptic encephalopathies (DEEs) (variant found in children)
claims.quote: the gene variant Kcnb1R312H (R312H mice) found in children with developmental and epileptic encephalopathies (DEEs)

claims.object_text: R312H mice exhibit a phenotype similar to KCNB1 null mice
claims.quote: The R312H mice exhibited a similar phenotype to the null mice.
Wild type (WT) and R312H KCNB1 channels made complexes with integrins α5β5 (Integrin_K+ channel_Complexes, IKCs)

claims.object_text: impaired IKC biochemical signaling in R312H brains
claims.quote: whose biochemical signaling was impaired in R312H brains.

claims.object_text: Treatment with Angiotensin II in vitro corrected the neuronal abnormalities
claims.quote: Treatment with Angiotensin II in vitro, an agonist of Focal Adhesion kinase, a key component of IKC signaling machinery, corrected the neuronal abnormalities.

claims.object_text: mutation induces neuromorphological abnormalities through non-conducting mechanisms
claims.quote: a genetic mutation in a K+ channel induces severe neuromorphological abnormalities through non-conducting mechanisms
